alyssa (support): bumping this escalation from the customer — they saw the action fire twice when the assistant attempted a tool call and then fell back. ticket #2467 attached. logs and repro below. :frowning_face:

maria (customer): yes — our users got two confirmation emails and two invoices. they were charged twice. this is high-severity for us.

alyssa (support): repro steps from the customer pasted: 
1) user asks assistant to ‘send invoice’
2) assistant triggers toolcall to /send-invoice (tool schema validated client-side)
3) call returned 202 Accepted quickly
4) frontend retried after timeout -> second toolcall executed -> fallback path also triggered -> plain-text fallback triggered another send

maria (customer): attaching the request payload and the delivery log snippet: 
```
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "input": "send invoice to john@acme.com",
  "tool_call": {"name": "send_invoice", "args": {"email": "john@acme.com", "amount": 99}}
}
```

maria (customer): delivery log (timestamps redacted): 
```
[2023-11-02T14:03:21Z] -> POST /v1/tool/send_invoice -> 202 Accepted
[2023-11-02T14:03:28Z] -> POST /v1/tool/send_invoice -> 200 OK (exec)
[2023-11-02T14:03:28Z] -> fallback exec -> send_email() executed
```

jeff (eng-runtime): thanks — initial read: two separate execution paths triggered. likely a retry client-side + late fallback path executed the tool action again. a few things to confirm: does the tool execution path require an idempotency token? customer payload looks missing an idempotency header.

lina (eng-oncall): I see traces for the session. here's the condensed trace (session id x-77a): 
```
14:03:21 - model -> tool-request queued -> engine returned ACCEPTED async
14:03:27 - client retry (timeout) -> new tool-request processed top-of-queue -> executed
14:03:27 - fallback detection: schema mismatch flagged after second exec -> fallback executor invoked -> fallback execution also triggers send_email() because tooling pipeline hasn't gated duplicate execs
```

jeff (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: our fallback code path will attempt a non-tool handler that can also call external actions. if the tool request was already enqueued but unresolved, fallback should NOT execute side-effecting actions. missing a guard + no idempotency in tool adapter.

cheng (billing): we have two invoice charges. customer is asking for immediate refund if confirmed. can eng confirm duplication source so we can reverse charges?

alyssa (support): customer wants a remediation timeline + repro steps that we can share with billing for refund.

jeff (eng-runtime): quick repro I ran locally: 
1) send toolcall without X-Idempotency-Key header
2) return 202 from runtime for first request (simulate slow worker)
3) client SDK sees no final status and retries -> runtime executes second request -> both requests call the tool adapter -> tool adapter executes side-effect 

curl example: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"send invoice","tool_call":{"name":"send_invoice","args":{"email":"a@b.com","amount":99}}}'
```

jeff (eng-runtime): log from adapter: 
```
[worker-9] Received tool execution request id=tn-abc123 intent=send_invoice
[worker-9] Executing send_invoice -> POST https://payments.internal/charge
[worker-9] Success -> 200 -> invoice_id=inv-999
```

jeff (eng-runtime): adapter didn't check for idempotency key; payments service processed both. runtime should attach/require idempotency header or hold fallback until final status.

lina (eng-oncall): quick mitigation we can ship in next patch: 1) gate fallback so it cannot perform side-effects unless tool execution is in final failed state (not just no response) 2) enforce X-Idempotency-Key presence at the API layer for toolcall-type requests -> return 400 if missing. that will prevent client retries from double-exec.

cheng (billing): we'll freeze refunds pending confirmation of duplicate execs. please tag which invoice ids to refund once confirmed.

alyssa (support): assigned to jeff+lina for root cause + a hotfix. cheng will prepare refund once we confirm invoice ids. mariA (customer) — asking if you can share the two invoice ids from your side so billing can cross-check?

maria (customer): yes, invoice ids inv-999 and inv-1000. refunds please. also: can you confirm whether this will be fixed soon? we need assurance to restore customer trust.

jeff (eng-runtime): timeline: implement fallback gating + idempotency header enforcement. I'll open a quick PR to validate header at the API ingress and short-circuit fallback execution. target hotfix within 48 hours, can push a rollback-safe toggle. :thumbsup:

lina (eng-oncall): I'll draft the revert-safe change: config flag enable_strict_tool_idempotency default=false -> will flip to true for the hotfix rollout in staging, then prod once validated.

cheng (billing): once eng confirms inv-999 is a duplicate we will issue immediate refund and notify customer.

alyssa (support): thanks all. action items: 
- jeff: PR to require X-Idempotency-Key + adapter check (48h)
- lina: patch to prevent fallback from executing side-effects when tool is pending (48h)
- cheng: hold refunds until eng confirms duplicate trace
- maria: please paste any additional logs or timestamps if available

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-87 (severity 2) — assigned: eng-runtime, eng-oncall, billing.

maria (customer): thank you. appreciate the fast response.

alyssa (support): marking as escalated -> will post progress updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
